description: Real-world crew-currency regulations are role-specific: a pilot's medical/BFR/instrument/135-check requirements (14 CFR Part 61 and 135) do not apply to a mechanic (14 CFR Part 65 A&P/IA requirements apply instead) or to a Dispatch ops-coordinator (no personal FAA currency certificate requirement applies to this codebase's 'dispatcher' role, which is a general operations-coordination duty, not the FAA-certificated Aircraft Dispatcher credential under 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart C — see dispatcherNote below). Extracted 2026-09-08 after a live smoke test found the crew-currency engine evaluating every crew member against the full pilot-currency checklist regardless of role, producing false 'expired/missing' results for non-pilots. This ruleset is the single source of truth for which regulatory currency checks apply to which duty role and their real thresholds — services/dispatch/crewQualsEngine.js reads roleCurrencyRequirements below programmatically rather than hardcoding a per-role check list in JS.

pilot.citationNote: 14 CFR Part 61 (and Part 135 for on-demand charter/air-taxi operators, the default assumption for this platform's crew-legality engine per crewQualsEngine.js's CFR_135_267_FLOOR).

checks.label: Day passenger-carrying currency
checks.threshold: 3 takeoffs and 3 landings (any type) as sole manipulator of the controls within the preceding 90 days, to carry passengers.

checks.label: Night passenger-carrying currency
checks.threshold: 3 takeoffs and 3 FULL-STOP landings within the preceding 90 days, during the period beginning 1 hour after sunset and ending 1 hour before sunrise, to carry passengers at night. Distinct from day currency above — a pilot can hold one and not the other; this codebase previously collapsed both into one day-only check, which is incorrect.

checks.label: Instrument currency
checks.threshold: 6 instrument approaches, holding procedures, and intercepting/tracking courses through navigational electronic systems within the preceding 6 calendar months, to act as PIC under IFR or in weather conditions below VFR minimums. A pilot outside this window has an additional 6-calendar-month 'grace period' (61.57(c)(3)) before an Instrument Proficiency Check (IPC, 61.57(d)) is required to reestablish currency — this ruleset's engine treats the base 6-month window as the GREEN/YELLOW/RED boundary and does not separately model the grace period; flag rather than silently apply it.

checks.label: Medical certificate
checks.threshold: Duration depends on medical class AND age at exam AND the class of operation being conducted (61.23(d) full table below) — this platform stores the pilot's own self-reported real expiration date rather than computing one from class+age, so the correct duration is whatever the pilot's actual FAA-issued certificate states. Reference table only, for sanity-checking an entered date, not for computing one: First-class — 12 calendar months (ATP ops) if under 40 at exam, 6 months if 40+; 12 months for commercial-privilege ops regardless of age. Second-class — 12 months for commercial-privilege ops regardless of age. Third-class (or unused portion of 1st/2nd class) for private/recreational/student ops — 60 months if under 40 at exam, 24 months if 40+. A self-reported expiration date more than 60 months from the exam/report date is not possible under any class/age combination and should be treated as a data-entry error, not a fact.

checks.label: Flight review (BFR)
checks.threshold: Every 24 calendar months, from an authorized instructor (or an accepted alternative such as a phase of the FAA WINGS program or a proficiency check), to act as PIC.

checks.label: Instrument Proficiency Check (61.57(d))
checks.threshold: Required to reestablish instrument currency once both the 6-month currency window and its 6-month grace period have lapsed. Tracked here as its own 6-calendar-month-cadence event distinct from `instrumentCurrency` above (the raw approach/hold tally) — see file header note in pilotCurrency.js.

checks.label: 135.293 competency check / 135.351 recurrent training
checks.threshold: Annual (12 calendar months) competency check and recurrent ground/flight training for pilots in Part 135 operations. ASSUMPTION, stated explicitly: this codebase has no per-tenant signal distinguishing Part 91 vs. Part 135 operating rules (docs/CODEX-aviation-suite.md describes an `operationCategory` branch that does not actually exist anywhere in the code as of this ruleset's authoring) — this platform defaults conservatively to treating all pilot crew as Part 135, consistent with crewQualsEngine.js's existing CFR_135_267_FLOOR default. A pure Part 91 operator would not actually be subject to this check; that distinction is not yet modeled.

checks.label: 135.297 instrument proficiency check
checks.threshold: Every 6 calendar months for pilots conducting Part 135 IFR operations — same Part-135-default assumption as typeRecurrent above applies.

mx.citationNote: 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart D (Mechanics) and Subpart E (Inspection Authorization) — NOT the Part 61/135 pilot requirements above. A mechanic was never required to hold a medical certificate, BFR, or any pilot currency item; evaluating one against those checks is a modeling error, not a real gap in their record.

checks.label: A&P recent experience
checks.threshold: To exercise the privileges of an Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) certificate, a mechanic must have, within the preceding 24 months, either worked at least 6 months maintaining aircraft in the certificate's rating(s), or passed an approved refresher/competency exam — commonly summarized as '24 of the preceding 36 months' of recent maintenance experience. If neither condition is met, 65.83 requires demonstrating ability to a qualified inspector before exercising the certificate's privileges again.

checks.label: Inspection Authorization (IA) renewal
checks.threshold: An IA is renewed annually (each March, on the anniversary structure FAA Order 8900.1 describes), contingent on meeting one of the real activity thresholds in 65.93(a) (e.g. performed at least 1 annual inspection for each 90 days held, or performed/supervised at least 2 major repairs, or attended an approved IA refresher course, or passed a written test) during the preceding 12 months. Distinct from, and in addition to, holding a current A&P — a mechanic can be a current A&P without a current IA, and vice versa is not possible (IA requires an underlying current A&P).

dispatcher.citationNote: This codebase's 'dispatcher' duty role (services/scheduling/crewScheduling.js VALID_ROLES) represents a general flight-operations/dispatch-coordination duty, not the FAA-certificated Aircraft Dispatcher credential under 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart C. Confirmed by inspection: nothing in this codebase issues, tracks, or references an Aircraft Dispatcher certificate number or the Part 65 Subpart C training/currency requirements that would attach to one. If a future tenant's dispatch staff DO hold that certificate, this ruleset does not yet model its currency requirements (recentcy of dispatch experience under 65.59, etc.) — that would need to be added as a real, separately-cited addition, not assumed to already be covered here.
dispatcher.dispatcherNote: No personal FAA regulatory currency requirement applies to this role as currently modeled in this codebase. Do not surface blocking or red items against a dispatcher for pilot-only or mechanic-only currency checks.

hard_stops.label: Never apply one duty role's currency requirements to a crew member in a different duty role
hard_stops.logic: A pilot's medical/BFR/instrument/135-check requirements (14 CFR 61/135) and a mechanic's A&P/IA requirements (14 CFR 65) are legally distinct requirement sets tied to distinct certificates. Applying one role's checklist to a different role produces a false 'expired/missing' determination — this is not a conservative error, it's an incorrect one, since the requirement was never real for that person.
hard_stops.trigger: AI (or the underlying evaluateCrewMember computation) reports a pilot-only currency item (medical, BFR, IPC, 61.57 recency, 135.293/135.297) as expired, missing, or a blocking item for a crew member whose role is 'mx' or 'dispatcher'; or reports an A&P/IA item against a 'pilot' or 'dispatcher'.
hard_stops.on_fail: Only surface the currency checks listed for that crew member's actual role in roleCurrencyRequirements above; for 'dispatcher', state plainly that no personal regulatory currency requirement applies rather than showing blank/expired fields.

hard_stops.label: Never state a currency threshold, calendar window, or regulation citation not present in this ruleset or a verified primary FAA source
hard_stops.logic: Currency thresholds are precise regulatory facts (exact day/month counts, exact CFR sections) — an approximate or misremembered number is not a safe substitute and could understate a real requirement.
hard_stops.trigger: AI states a specific currency threshold or citation for a duty role/check not listed in roleCurrencyRequirements above.
hard_stops.on_fail: State that this specific threshold isn't in the current ruleset and should be verified against the actual CFR text or the tenant's own OpSpec/GOM before being relied on.

soft_flags.label: 135.293/135.297 checks are applied to every pilot by conservative default, since this codebase has no real per-tenant Part 91 vs. 135 operating-rules signal
soft_flags.logic: docs/CODEX-aviation-suite.md describes an operationCategory branch (Part 135 standard / HEMES / Part 91) that does not exist in the actual code as of this ruleset — the default-conservative Part 135 assumption elsewhere in crewQualsEngine.js (CFR_135_267_FLOOR) is extended here for consistency, not because every tenant is confirmed Part 135.
soft_flags.trigger: A pilot's typeRecurrent or ipc297 check is surfaced as blocking or flagged.
soft_flags.message: This check assumes Part 135 operations by platform default — confirm this tenant's actual operating rules if that assumption may not hold.

soft_flags.label: Medical certificate expiration is the pilot's own self-reported date, not independently computed from class/age/exam date
soft_flags.logic: See roleCurrencyRequirements.pilot.checks[medical].threshold's reference table — this platform trusts the self-reported expiration date rather than recomputing it, since it has no verified exam date or birthdate on file for most pilots.
soft_flags.trigger: A medical certificate currency band is surfaced.
soft_flags.message: Medical expiration is self-reported by the pilot, not independently verified against the real 61.23(d) duration table — sanity-check against the actual FAA-issued certificate.

disclaimer: Crew currency checks in this platform are computed per duty role from real logged flights and self-reported currency events (pilots) or self-reported maintenance/inspection-authorization events (mechanics), governed by this ruleset's role-to-requirement mapping. No personal FAA currency check is modeled for the Dispatch ops-coordination role. Part 135-specific pilot checks (135.293/135.297) are applied by conservative platform default in the absence of a real per-tenant Part 91/135 signal. All Mode B (self-reported) currency data is tagged as such and is not independently attested by an instructor, AME, or IA inspector at source.
system_context: You are governed by av_crew_currency_v0: pilot currency requirements (14 CFR 61.56, 61.57(a)(1)/(a)(2)/(c)/(d), 61.23, 135.293, 135.297) apply ONLY to crew members with role 'pilot'. Mechanic currency requirements (14 CFR 65.83 A&P recent experience, 65.93/65.91 IA renewal) apply ONLY to role 'mx'. The 'dispatcher' role in this codebase has no personal FAA regulatory currency requirement modeled — never state or imply a dispatcher's currency is expired, missing, or a compliance gap for a pilot- or mechanic-only requirement. Never invent a currency threshold or CFR citation not listed in this ruleset's roleCurrencyRequirements.
